pa.structure_note: A Professional Association (PA) is a genuinely distinct Texas entity type, not a synonym for Professional Corporation (PC). CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against Texas Business Organizations Code Chapter 302, the Texas Legislature's own statute text, and the Secretary of State's own Form 204 instructions: (1) A PA is restricted to a specific, narrow list of professions -- Texas law limits PA formation to the professional service rendered by a doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy, doctor of podiatry, dentist, chiropractor, optometrist, therapeutic optometrist, veterinarian, or licensed mental health professional. This is NOT a general-purpose vehicle the way PLLC or PC are for any licensed profession -- a DDV tenant should only be classified as 'pa' if their profession is actually on this list. (2) A PA can issue stock, but the stockholders are called 'members,' not 'shareholders,' and a PA is explicitly NOT a true corporation despite operating under corporate-law provisions (Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 302.001 applies Chapters 20/21 for-profit corporation provisions unless they conflict with Title 7). (3) Only a member of the association is eligible to serve as an officer or governing person (Section 302.008(a)) -- a stricter, PA-specific rule with no direct equivalent in the PC file.

identity: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status
governance: Member Voting Records (per Certificate of Formation, Section 302.006)
statutory: Texas Business Organizations Code Chapter 302 Compliance
Texas Business Organizations Code Chapter 301 Compliance (professional-entity ownership/licensing restrictions)
Texas Franchise Tax Public Information Report (PIR) Filing
Foreign Qualification Filings (if operating in other states)
professional_licensing_compliance: Profession Eligibility Confirmation (PA restricted to the professions listed in Section 302.001 et seq. -- see structure_note)
Individual Professional License Verification (Officers -- must also be members, per Section 302.008(a))
Entity Name Compliance Certification (professional designator and governing-profession ethics-rule check)
State Licensing Board Registration (e.g. Texas Medical Board, State Board of Dental Examiners, Texas Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners, depending on the specific profession)
Single-Profession-Type Confirmation (Section 2.004 -- a professional entity may generally engage in only one type of professional service, with limited statutory exceptions)

Certificate of Formation (Professional A: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 1, Chapter 3, Subchapter A (general formation) and Title 7, Chapter 302 (PA-specific provisions) -- filed via Secretary of State Form 204, distinct from the PC Form 203 and PLLC Form 206. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 204 instructions.
Profession Eligibility Confirmation (PA: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 302.001 read with the Form 204 instructions' own enumerated list: a professional association may only be formed for the professional service rendered by a doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy, doctor of podiatry, dentist, chiropractor, optometrist, therapeutic optometrist, veterinarian, or licensed mental health professional. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 204 instructions -- this is the single most important gating fact for whether the 'pa' entity type applies to a given tenant at all.
Officer Appointments (members only, per: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 302.008(a): only a member of the professional association is eligible to serve as an officer or governing person. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against Texas Legislature statute text (statutes.capitol.texas.gov).
Member Voting Records (per Certificate o: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 302.006: a member's voting rights are governed by the association's own Certificate of Formation, not a fixed statutory default the way corporate shareholder voting often is.
Texas Business Organizations Code Chapte: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 7, Chapter 302, applying Chapters 20 and 21 (for-profit corporation provisions) except where they conflict with Title 7 (Section 302.001). CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against Texas Legislature statute text.

Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 301.001(a) confirms Title 7 (including Chapter 301's ownership/licensing restrictions) applies to professional associations, professional corporations, and PLLCs alike -- explicitly excluding partnerships and LLPs (Section 301.001(c)).
